fullExplanation.text: Understanding Ignatius, Justin, Irenaeus, Trent, and Vatican II

Within Eucharist, the question Ignatius, Justin, Irenaeus, Trent, and Vatican II must be answered at the right level of authority. Develops the biblical, liturgical, patristic, conciliar, and philosophical account of sacrifice, memorial, Real Presence, transubstantiation, communion, and adoration. Scripture, ecclesial teaching, historical testimony, and specialist research contribute different kinds of evidence. The lesson therefore identifies which source establishes each premise and labels every interpretive step rather than presenting a synthesis as though it were a direct quotation.

fullExplanation.response: The Catholic response to Ignatius, Justin, Irenaeus, Trent, and Vatican II is cumulative and limited. essentialTerminology.definition: The sacrament of Christ's Body and Blood, the memorial of his Passover, sacrificial banquet, and source of ecclesial communion.
The change of the whole substance of bread and wine into Christ's Body and Blood while sensible appearances remain.
Communion in holy things and among holy persons in Christ across the pilgrim, purifying, and glorified Church.

scriptureEvidence.paraphrase: Jesus presents himself as the life-giving bread from heaven and presses his hearers beyond merely material expectations.
At the Passover meal Jesus identifies the bread and cup with his self-gift and commands the memorial action of the new covenant.
Paul joins Eucharistic participation to communion in Christ, ecclesial unity, received tradition, and serious moral discernment.
